### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **70** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c93f8807e0ed8410b1cafef58adc42763fb6740`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c93f8807e0ed8410b1cafef58adc42763fb6740` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7abd4bb5353008ee2b3a8bf31ac5925b3fabaca0` — the merge of head `5e11588a704209e1fa6e02c4fdd08b89548dc924` into base `4c93f8807e0ed8410b1cafef58adc42763fb6740`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7abd4bb5353008ee2b3a8bf31ac5925b3fabaca0 && git checkout 7abd4bb5353008ee2b3a8bf31ac5925b3fabaca0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4c93f8807e0ed8410b1cafef58adc42763fb6740 5e11588a704209e1fa6e02c4fdd08b89548dc924 && git checkout -B drift-repro 4c93f8807e0ed8410b1cafef58adc42763fb6740 && git merge --no-ff 5e11588a704209e1fa6e02c4fdd08b89548dc924

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4c93f8807e0ed8410b1cafef58adc42763fb6740
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 4c93f8807e0ed8410b1cafef58adc42763fb6740` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4f2ffd2dcb5372c9a2324cd6730c0e5db0ac0bee`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-project/evals/project-process.json, skills/objectstack-project/references/platform-catalog.md + packages/formula/src/working-day.ts, packages/formula/src/working-day-needs.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-to-filter.ts, packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts, packages/formula/src/types.ts, packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/objectql/src/formula-work-calendars.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-find.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts, packages/spec/scripts/lib/platform-catalog.ts, ui/packages/core/src/evaluator/formulaRecord.ts
Security-touching: no

Inputs read: card #35356 (body and its four comments: unblock 7011103158, shipping note 7054955353, grade note 7063199719, claim 7101714597), PR #36796 (body, the dev report 7118578527, the docs-drift comment, the review claim), the net diff against `main` at this head, ADR-0157 and AGENTS.md on `main`, and the 70 check-runs on this head: 61 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed (Test Core 1-10, Test UI 1-16, the type-check and lint families, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness all green). Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- Expression accept set, formula sites: `addWorkingDays`, `workingDaysBetween`, `addWorkingHours` become callable in a `formula` field's and a stored field's `expression` (two-argument and three-argument overloads, `working-day.ts#registerWorkingDayFunctions`). On `main` each was an unknown function and failed the build. Widening. Right, and it is ADR-0157 D4's own scope.
- Expression accept set, every other linted site: the three are refused by `validate-expressions.ts#refuseWorkingDayElsewhere` in `check()`, the declared flow predicate slot and the declared flow value slot. They were refused there before (unknown function), so nothing an author could write is taken away. Not a narrowing. Right. One site is missed: see S1.
- Calendar code must be a quoted literal (`working-day-needs.ts#computedCalendarCodeMessage`, called from `judgeFieldFormula`). A refusal on a surface that is new in this diff. Right, and forced by the design: the calendars are loaded from the calls the source spells, before a synchronous evaluation.
- `CEL_STDLIB_FUNCTIONS` (published, `@objectstack/formula`) gains three names. Widening of a published list. Right; the skill-catalog pin is green on this head.
- `EvalContext.workCalendars` (optional), `EvalWorkCalendar`, `EvalWorkCalendars`, and the index exports `WORKING_DAY_FUNCTIONS`, `WorkingDayFunction`, `workCalendarsNotLoadedMessage`, `callsWorkingDayFunction`, `workingDayCalendarNeeds`, `computedCalendarCodeMessage`, `WorkingDayCalendarNeeds`: additive public surface of `@objectstack/formula`. Right. Absent `workCalendars` throws, it does not count: this holds D2 (no wall-clock fallback) for every caller that predates the field.
- Filter compilation: `cel-to-filter.ts#refuseWorkingDayCall` keeps the reason code `unsupported` and changes only the detail text, at the two `default` branches that already threw. No accept-set change. Right (D6).
- Read and write values: a formula that calls one reads a value where it could not exist before; a refused calendar reads `null` with one fault line (D8). A stored `expression` that meets the refusal stores `null` and the write goes through: this is the pre-existing answer of `computeStoredExpressions` for any expression that does not evaluate (#24619 docblock on `main`), not a new branch. Right; judged as open point 1 in ③.
- Write-path validator and the Console form: a working-day formula joins the unservable set on both sides (`engine-top-level.ts#unservableReason`, `formulaRecord.ts#planObjectFormulas`). Right, and it is the ADR's own Consequences line for the Console.
- Platform catalog: the "Working-day formulas" row leaves `PLANNED_ROWS` and the generated page, and `sys_work_calendar`'s reach names the formulas. Generator and generated page agree string for string. Eval 8 flips from `PLATFORM-CANDIDATE` to `addWorkingHours(`. Both are the two steps note 7054955353 on the card requires of the shipping PR. Right.
- No spec schema, no authorable key and no `authorable-surface` shard moves; the only `packages/spec` change is the unpublished generator row list. Right as a reading of the tree. It does not settle the `Metadata-protocol` kind: see ②.

### ② Semver level

M1 (must-fix) — `Metadata-protocol: none` with `@objectstack/formula: patch` does not match what the diff publishes.

- AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3: `Metadata-protocol` is "the change to what a metadata author can write — a new key, accepted value or metadata type is `added`", and "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, `none` takes `patch`".
- What this diff publishes: an author may now write `addWorkingDays(...)`, `workingDaysBetween(...)` and `addWorkingHours(...)` in a field's `expression`, where the build refused each as an unknown function before. That is a new accepted value in an authorable slot. The PR body's ground for `none` ("no authorable key, no `authorable-surface/**` shard moves") reads the rule as keys only; the rule also names accepted values.
- Direct precedent on `main`, one week old and the same kind of change: #34433 (`rmbUpper`), changeset `34332-formula-rmb-upper.md`: `Metadata-protocol: added — a formula, predicate or flow value may now call rmbUpper(...)`, with `'@objectstack/formula': minor`.
- The sibling #35355 service changeset is `none` at `patch` correctly: it exported arithmetic and a service, and no formula could call anything yet. This PR is the one that opens the authorable surface.
- Fix: `Metadata-protocol: added` in the PR body and in the changeset body, and `@objectstack/formula` at least `minor`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right and stays. The other four packages carry no protocol kind of their own in this diff (`@objectstack/lint` refuses nothing that was accepted before; `@objectstack/objectql` and `@object-ui/core` add behaviour behind the new functions; `@objectstack/skills` is teaching text); whether any of them is "moved" by the kind in the rule's sense is the dev's to state when the level is corrected.
- The Check Changeset run is green; it checks that a changeset exists and is well formed, and cannot derive the kind.

The rest of ② holds: a changeset exists for every released package the diff touches, no `skip-changeset`, no narrowing arm, no BREAKING banner owed, and the "not released alone" line names its pair (#35355, #35357) as ADR-0157 D4 requires.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question, open point 1 (a stored `expression` that meets a D8 refusal). ADR-0157 leaves it to this review ("the card named settles each under its own contract review"; not a maintainer question). Answered: **option A stands — the field stores blank and the write goes through, with the fault line.** Grounds, from the ADR and the tree, not from the PR body:
  - It is what every stored `expression` already does when it does not evaluate (`computeStoredExpressions`, #24619). Option B would make a calendar refusal the one fault that fails a write, a second semantic for one function family.
  - D8 rules the read: blank, one line, never a guess. A stored column and a computed one then answer alike for the same calendar state.
  - D9 records why a blocking refusal was not offered for approvals: with D8 it would block every record whose span crosses the year end until next year's holidays are entered. The same holds for every case opened in late December.
  - D2 is kept: the stored value is blank, never a weekly-pattern or wall-clock count. The ADR-0144 D5 precedent D8 cites is the same shape (no fallback value stored).
  - Two consequences the decision carries, both to be stated where authors read (the docs page says the first only by implication): a blank stored due time stays blank until that record's next write, since nothing recomputes it when the calendar is fixed; and a later write recomputes, so a record whose stored due time was valid is blanked by an unrelated edit made while its calendar refuses. A filter such as "due before now" never matches a blank, so an escalation built on the stored column is silent for those rows. This is the price of A and is consistent with the ADR's Consequences ("An unmaintained calendar blanks deadlines"); the Setup notice of D8 is the mitigation. No change to the code is asked.
- Dev flag, calendar code as a quoted literal: accepted, see ①.
- Dev flag, blank handling (blank start answers blank; blank count or blank end refuses): accepted as D4's "the card's to settle", pinned in `working-day.test.ts`.
- Dev flag, no hook sandbox host function: accepted. The card says "if the sandbox needs" one; a hook reads the stored field.
- Dev flag, contract-review tier ("the seat decides"): the three `skills/**` paths put the PR on the rules face, so this record is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` whatever the spec criterion reads.
- Dev flag, file surface beyond the order's list (objectql engine facets, `packages/lint`, `ui/packages/core`): each is where the contract is implemented or enforced; in scope above.
- Dev report `security_findings: "withheld"`: nothing for this record to answer; no changed hunk in the `hits` files teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour, hence `Security-touching: no`.
- Rule change: no `.claude/**` path in the diff; not applicable.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The diff adds at most one default resolution and one resolution per quoted code, per organization, per read, through the calendar service's cache, and only when a planned expression names a working-day function (`planWorkCalendarNeeds`). The arithmetic runs in memory because ADR-0157 D6 rules it so ("No calendar math runs in SQL"). No finding.
- Release pairing (D4): the changeset says it is not released alone and names #35355 and #35357, whose changesets are pending on `main`. Held.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md`** — against the spec it teaches. The Working days paragraph agrees with `working-day.ts`: the three signatures, the default calendar without a code, the quoted-literal code, formula or stored `expression` only, and the stored `datetime` field as the way to filter (D6). All three names are in `CEL_STDLIB_FUNCTIONS`, and the catalog-sync pin is green. One sentence overclaims: "refused elsewhere" (S1). The token budget was paid by deleting text elsewhere in the file; most of it is restatement, two pieces are not (N1).

**`skills/objectstack-project/evals/project-process.json`** — eval 8 against the card and the catalog. The prompt asks for a business-hours SLA formula; the expected answer (no app calendar objects, `addWorkingHours(record.opened_at, 8)` on the default calendar or a quoted code, stored in a `datetime` field with an `expression` because a filter cannot run calendar arithmetic, `escalation.clock: 'working_time'` for an approval step) is what the tree does, and the assertions (`sys_work_calendar`, `addWorkingHours(`; no `PLATFORM-CANDIDATE`, no `PLATFORM-GAP`) are the flip note 7054955353 asks for. Holds, with N3 and N4.

**`skills/objectstack-project/references/platform-catalog.md`** and **`packages/spec/scripts/lib/platform-catalog.ts`** — generated page and generator agree; the Planned row is gone from both; no other skill file on this head still says no formula reads a calendar. Holds.

**`packages/formula/src/working-day.ts`, `stdlib.ts`, `types.ts`, `cel-engine.ts`, `validate.ts`, `index.ts`** — against ADR-0157 D2, D4, D8, D11. Every count goes through `work-calendar.ts` (the module on `main` the service and the approval clock use): no second walk and no second wall-clock rule, which is open point 3's requirement. `calendarFor` throws when no map, no default entry or no entry for the code was handed over, and rethrows a refusal held as data; no path counts without a resolved calendar. The docblock's contract (start excluded, end included, `0` answers the start, a day read on the UTC calendar, an instant for hours) matches `work-calendar.ts#addWorkingDays`, `#workingDaysBetween`, `#addWorkingHours` sentence by sentence. `types.ts` states "absent is not refused" and the code does that. Holds, with N5.

**`packages/formula/src/working-day-needs.ts`** — the AST walk reads the two-argument form as the default, a `value` string third argument as a code, and anything else as computed; the regex pre-scan only gates the parse. A string literal that spells a call matches the pre-scan and then finds no call node, so it answers `undefined`. Holds.

**`packages/formula/src/cel-to-filter.ts`** — D6. `lowerCondition` and `classify` have no `call` case, so every working-day call reaches a `default` branch and gets the named refusal with reason `unsupported`; another function keeps the generic text (pinned as a control). Holds, with N3 on the wording.

**`packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`** — D6's lint. The refusal runs at `check()` (validation rules, field rules, option `visibleWhen`, action `visible` / `disabled` / `pressed`, app landing, sharing rules, hook conditions) and at the declared flow predicate and value slots; `judgeFieldFormula` accepts the call and refuses a computed code. The runtime publish gate runs the same rules.

S1 (should-fix) — an expression `defaultValue` is not a refused site, and the published text says it is.
- The claim: SKILL.md "Formula or stored `expression` only, refused elsewhere"; the lint docblock "Every other expression site ... is handed no calendar".
- The tree: `validate-expressions.ts` never walks a field's expression `defaultValue` (its only reads of `defaultValue` are the nullability premise near line 557), and no other file in `packages/lint/src` validates one. The names are registered unconditionally, so a `defaultValue` written as the CEL expression `addWorkingDays(today(), 3)` type-checks and builds green.
- At run time `engine-defaults-and-autonumbers.ts` evaluates the default with no `workCalendars`, the call throws, and the branch logs `Failed to evaluate default expression` and leaves the field unset: every insert, a blank due date and one warn line. "A due date defaulting to three working days from today" is the most natural wrong site for these functions, and D6's lint exists "so an author learns this when writing the expression". Seed `cel` values are evaluated the same way (`seed-eval.ts#resolveSeed`) and are not walked by the lint either.
- Not a must-fix: the result is blank, never a wrong-clock value, so D2 holds.
- Fix: refuse the three at an expression `defaultValue` (and a seed value) with the stored-`expression` prescription, or state in the skill and the lint docblock exactly which sites are refused. The first is what D6 asks for.

**`packages/objectql/src/formula-work-calendars.ts`, `engine-find.ts`, `engine-insert.ts`, `engine-update.ts`, `engine-top-level.ts`** — D2, D4, D8 and open point 4. The service is reused (one cache, one refusal vocabulary); a refusal is settled into data and thrown by the function, so the existing fault sink writes the one line; a kernel with no service refuses with the service's own error rather than counting. `applyFormulaPlan` binds per row, so two organizations in one page each count with their own default (pinned). The fallback to `context.tenantId` when the row carries no `organization_id` is sound where it applies: a read that carries a tenant is confined to it, which is the same premise the service's own elevated read relies on.

S2 (should-fix) — the answer depends on whether the projection kept `organization_id`.
- `resolveFormulaWorkCalendars` reads the organization off the row, else off the context. `planFormulaProjection` widens a projection with the fields an expression reads, and `organization_id` is not one of them.
- So a read that carries no tenant (a system read across organizations) with `fields: ['id', 'due_day']` hands rows without `organization_id`: outside the `single` posture every such row is refused `no_organization` and reads blank, while the same row reads its value when the projection is omitted or names `organization_id`. The module header states this outcome; it does not state that the projection decides it.
- It is a refusal, not a wrong calendar, so not a must-fix. But a formula's value must not depend on which sibling columns the caller selected.
- Fix: when the plan names a working-day function, add `organization_id` to the widened fetch on objects that declare it (the existing `widened` mechanism), so the row always names its organization.
- Read in the code, not run.

`computeStoredExpressions` passes the calendars to the same `applyFormulaPlan` and stores what it answers: open point 1 as ruled in ③. `unservableReason` names the new case. Holds otherwise.

**`ui/packages/core/src/evaluator/formulaRecord.ts`** — the form marks a working-day formula unservable, as the ADR's Consequences require and as the server's write-path check does. Holds.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):
- N1 — SKILL.md: "(translations: table below)" follows a sentence naming `PRIOR()`, and the translation table has no `PRIOR` row (it has `OLD.x` and `ISBLANK(x)`); the deleted sentence was the file's only `PRIOR()` to `previous.x` mapping. The deleted built-ins sentence also carried "`+ duration(…)` included; shift a date with `isoDate(addDays(record.d, n))`" for a `date` field, which no remaining line says. The PR body calls the deletions restatement; these two are not.
- N2 — SKILL.md does not say that a call reads blank when the organization has no default calendar or the count passes the maintained span, nor that the start day is excluded and the end included. The docs page says both; the skill is one token under its ceiling.
- N3 — `now()` against `{now}`: eval 8's expected output and the lint message say the stored field is compared with `now()`; the compiler's refusal says `{now}`. In a query filter the instant is spelled `{now}` (ADR-0157 D6; `skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md`), `now()` is right only in a CEL condition evaluated in memory, and a CEL source compiled to a filter lowers neither. One spelling per site would read better.
- N4 — the catalog row says "`addWorkingDays()`-style formulas" while eval 8 asserts `addWorkingHours(`; the name is reachable only through the project skill's routing to objectstack-formula. Naming the three in the row would close it.
- N5 — `working-day.ts`: the calendar is resolved before the blank-start check, so a blank start on an organization whose calendar refuses still throws and writes the fault line; the value is blank either way.

M1 is a FAIL. S1 and S2 each earn a delta review of their fix.

- **S3 (should-fix, L1)** — the production wiring has no test. `plugin.ts` installs the service into a module-level `WeakMap` keyed by `this.ql`, and every formula path looks it up by its host's `facade`. If the key and the facade ever stop being the same object (a wrapper, a proxy, a re-created engine), every working-day formula silently reads blank with a refusal log. The value of the feature depends on that one handoff (l1-review-checklist 〈断言与收益〉).
